title: Not singing, and doing a single after the Savoy closed
summary: He did not sing with his own band; on a single in Toronto audiences wanted him to sing and sit in with bad pickup groups.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, I know something else that we haven't said. In what numbers were you singing with your own band?
None at all. I don't like my singing.
Cootie. All the numbers you sang with Duke, and you didn't sing any with your own band?
No. I don't like my singing.

Well, that's funny you should say that, because you know what you said about Pearl, that an artist often doesn't know what they can do. Well, I mean the point is maybe you wouldn't consider yourself that you're a singer, because of course you're a trumpet player and not a singer. But what you had to offer was something -- it was something that pleased. It was funny, it was -- you brought something to it. And well, I liked it very much.
I'll tell you a funny thing.

I'll tell you a funny thing. When I was out doing a single, I was up in Toronto, at one of the nightclubs up there, one of the spots up there, doing a single, and I had to learn about four songs. And the public, that's all they wanted me to do, was sing.
And I would tell them I didn't know no more songs. I was a trumpet player. I wasn't no singer.
And today, being an entertainer, a
jazz trumpet player, it's very hard. Just to be a jazz trumpet player.
You have to be an entertainer. On top of it, entertaining, telling jokes.
Not only blowing that trumpet. Don't care how much trumpet I can blow, they want me to entertain them, singing and dancing, and telling jokes.
Now, that's the business today. I found that out doing a single. That's one thing I wanted to say.
Yeah. Like, you mean, after the Savoy closed down.
Yeah. And did what, the Gale Agency send
And this is all they wanted from you, all this?
Well, did you have a band? Did you have a group?
No. I played with the group.
Whoever the group was, I played with the group and sang, rehearsed with them and sang with them.
And you certainly didn't like that, did you?
No. I lost about 14 pounds in one week.
Yes. And then have to submit to bad musicianship.
That's when I came back with the band.
That's when I came back with Duke's band.
Yeah. I mean, was the money that good, to justify it?
Yeah, the money was good, but as you said, playing with bad musicians.
They didn't know chord structure or nothing.

I'd be playing, maybe, 'Do Nothing Till You Hear From Me', and they'd be playing something else. You have to learn that in this business. See, the public is very funny. You're standing in front of the public out there, they don't want to know nothing about John Doe back there.
They're listening to you. I learned how to keep blowing, regardless of what them people are doing back there.
And I would finish my song, and I don't know where the hell they would be at.
Oh, that must be very depressing.
But all that's in the business, that you have to learn.
And a lot of people can't do that.
No. I know that. Well, now, wait a minute. Let's pause here a minute.
